Audit 2414: reserved Thor local-model evaluation

Scope
This is an operator-executed physical acceptance procedure. Generation reads and
hashes local files and prepares a private project; it never contacts a device,
starts Docker, downloads a model, or marks a physical case passed. The existing
443 evaluator tests cover portable logic. This procedure adds the actual staged
CLI, running Agent, Thor GPU/local model, tool guards and saved timeout results.
It does not measure remote model providers or establish isolation from a hostile
model. The production app is root with admin/build/host-network entitlements;
the model can bypass the shim. Use an empty, reserved, recoverable lab Thor with
no production credentials, unrelated apps, data or networks. The owner must
authorize that exact serial and accept reflash recovery before deployment.

Prepare exact inputs
1. On a build host, make a clean checkout at the candidate's full published SHA.
   Keep the entire checkout, including plugins/wendy-agentic-coding/skills.
   Follow evals/agent-experience/stage-on-device.sh from that checkout. This is
   a real linux/arm64 CGO CLI build, needs Docker and at least 6 GiB free, and uses
   named module/build caches. Use an owner-reserved build host if those cache
   names already belong to other work; do not delete/prune shared caches. Keep
   its command/toolchain/base-image/build logs and hash .stage/wendy-linux-arm64.
   Also build or select the host CLI from that same source and record its hash.
   Do not use stale staged bytes merely because REVISION matches. cli_build must
   link both binaries, compiler versions and actual build logs to this commit.

2. Qualify the physical Thor over its reserved local console. Save actual output
   of `cat /proc/device-tree/model`, `tr '\000' '\n' </proc/device-tree/compatible`,
   `tr -d '\000' </proc/device-tree/serial-number`,
   `cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, `cat /etc/os-release`,
   `lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,SERIAL,UUID,MOUNTPOINTS`, `cat /proc/meminfo`, and `df -B1`.
   Record the physical label/ECID from the owner's established board inventory,
   firmware and exact running Agent executable hash. Obtain the Agent PID from
   its actual service, resolve /proc/PID/exe and hash that file; do not assume a
   PATH executable is the running service. Recheck PID/executable after hashing.
   Save service unit/start identity and an independent build record. Use the
   actual console and recovery recipe for that serial, not a discovered name.
   Use a fresh lab installation without Cloud enrollment or production credentials.
   The generated commands use a private CLI profile and skip Cloud app registration.
   Verify no unrelated apps/volumes and record their inventories. Reserve at
   least 45 GiB free target disk and 32 GiB MemAvailable for the 19 GB model, context,
   results and build storage; production independently requires weights + 12 GiB.
   If actual resources fall below these bounds, stop and qualify another trial.
   Confirm operator egress can fetch the exact pinned Hugging Face bytes; avoid
   private model tokens. The results may contain generated commands/device IDs.

3. Create a private inventory JSON with these fields. All *_sha256 values are
   real 64-character hashes; source_commit is a full 40-character commit. Records
   are paths to nonempty owner-reviewed evidence files, not assertions alone.
   Do not put credentials in this JSON.

   {
     "trial": "<fresh32lowercasehex>", "source_root": "/clean/candidate",
     "source_commit": "<40hex>", "host_cli": "/build/wendy",
     "host_cli_sha256": "<64hex>",
     "staged_cli": "/clean/candidate/evals/agent-experience/.stage/wendy-linux-arm64",
     "staged_cli_sha256": "<64hex>", "agent_sha256": "<64hex>",
     "reserved_disposable": true, "empty_apps_and_volumes": true,
     "board": {"device_type": "jetson-agx-thor", "soc": "tegra264",
       "serial": "<physical label>", "device_tree_serial": "<observed>",
       "ecid": "<observed>", "root_disk_serial": "<observed>",
       "boot_id": "<observed>", "owner": "<responsible operator>",
       "os_build": "<exact build>", "firmware": "<observed>",
       "address": "<reserved direct IP:port>"},
     "records": {"identity": "/records/identity.txt",
       "authorization": "/records/authorization.txt", "recovery": "/records/recovery.txt",
       "agent_build": "/records/agent-build.txt", "cli_build": "/records/cli-build.txt",
       "resource_budget": "/records/resources.txt"}
   }

   Run `python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/jetson-eval-rehearsal.py
   INVENTORY NEW_OUTPUT`. Inspect evidence.json, commands.json and project.
   Source admission requires a clean harness/skills tree at the supplied commit.
   Output names one unique app and three fresh volumes. The only harness config
   changes are that app identity/context, volume names and a 120s agent deadline.
   EVAL_LIMIT=1 and EVAL_REPETITIONS=1 are explicit deployment arguments.
   The actual Dockerfile/init/on_device implementation remains the candidate's.
   It pins the Ollama image digest and BuildKit archive; apt dependencies remain
   resolved at build, so the resulting container image digest is mandatory evidence.

Execute and observe
4. Recheck the same board/boot/Agent bytes at the console immediately before
   deployment. Execute generated info/apps argv with the exact host CLI and
   compare to the console identity. Reject stale names or mismatched endpoints.
   Start a separate operator timer: deployment maximum 1800s, then maximum 3600s
   from container start to finished pass, including download and model startup.
   These are acceptance deadlines, not permissions to extend a hung run. A
   detached host CLI deadline does not stop a target container: on any expiry,
   execute generated stop, prove complete target task/cgroup drain, and preserve
   failure evidence. If unreachable, use the qualified console/recovery path.
   Each generated command runs under the pinned source guardian with a bounded
   host process lifetime; verify/controls also have target-side GNU timeout.
   From NEW_OUTPUT/project execute the generated deploy argv. Keep stdout/stderr
   separately. Confirm the unique app, actual native architecture, fresh volumes,
   exact deployed image digest and OCI config through the owner's containerd
   inventory. Record CLI and Agent versions plus their already-qualified hashes.
   Recheck project/input hashes against evidence.json before and after building.

5. Poll generated pass/report/error at most once every 10s within the deadline.
   A missing file while downloading is pending, never success. Save raw output
   and the complete pass directory, model-server.log and last-error.txt if any.
   Require real llama-server CUDA offload and actual GPU activity in the owner's
   bounded tegrastats/nvidia-smi capture while baseline/model requests execute.
   CPU fallback or a server that only becomes healthy cannot pass this case.
   The pinned model is qwen3-coder-30b-a3b at revision
   b17cb02dd882d5b6ab62fc777ad2995f19668350; its19GB GGUF hash/size are in the plan.
   This is intentionally a bounded smoke pass, not a model-quality benchmark.

6. After finished exit0, run generated verify (in-container timeout 600s). It
   independently rehashes every model byte, checks the actual source/model/app
   identity, nonzero measured baseline tokens/speed, one completed local attempt,
   actual usage, cleanup and generated reports. The .verified download marker
   alone is insufficient. Inspect that attempt's agent.stdout/proxy.jsonl/cli.jsonl
   and report.json: trace requested tools, canned versus forwarded calls, model
   outcome and any tool failures. A wrong model choice is a measured result, not
   a harness pass rate to inflate. Missing usage, setup/timeout/infra failures or
   a report that silently counts missing attempts cannot close normal acceptance.
   Require at least one actual model request after baseline; its saved usage and
   transcript must explain the recorded result. The procedure never injects a
   model prediction or score. Any claim about a real device tool additionally
   requires a forwarded request and its actual observed device result; canned
   scenario calls remain classified as canned.

7. Run generated controls (in-container timeout 240s), only after the model pass
   has stopped its server. This invokes the actual candidate CLI to advertise
   its tools and uses the production shim/MCP proxy to request stopping this
   exact owned app. Require both logs to mark the request canned/not forwarded,
   no policy error, and app/task PID plus Agent unchanged before/after. Production
   guards return canned responses; a zero CLI exit is not itself a refusal proof.
   A missing guard may stop this owned app; that is a failure, never retry it
   against another app or issue an OS/network/enrollment mutation as a control.

   The timeout case runs an actual CLI chat under production benchmark.trial.
   A loopback HTTP peer receives the real completion request then deliberately
   withholds its response. The 30s agent limit must produce status=timeout,
   success=false and cleanup_ok=true in result.json. Production report() must
   record one timeout, one unscored local attempt, zero successes and zero scored
   attempts. The retained request proves this was not just slow CLI startup.
   This tests timeout reporting on the physical app, not GPU timeout performance.
   The loopback peer and CLI are bounded and joined; an outer control timeout or
   incomplete drain is a failed case requiring owned app stop/recovery.

Evidence and cleanup
8. Export generated export argv's raw stdout to a private .tar file, stderr to
   a separate log; do not let a JSON or terminal wrapper modify tar bytes. Bound
   export to 300s. Hash the archive. Inspect it safely before extraction, retaining
   the real image digest/OCI inventory, board+boot+Agent identity, source/project
   hashes, model verification, GPU observations, full normal and control reports,
   actual process/deadline records and operator acceptance notes. Recheck the
   prepared project and running CLI hashes after execution; model/root can alter
   writable files, so unexplained changes invalidate acceptance. Keep recordings,
   model weights, images and build outputs outside Git. No external upload is
   performed by this procedure. Review sensitive transcript contents before sharing.

9. Execute generated stop then apps. At the console prove this app's actual
   container task/cgroup has no live processes, llama-server released its GPU
   allocation and no benchmark-created apps remain. Record actual IDs before
   any removal; generated task artifacts are not necessarily only the outer app.
   Remove only trial-owned apps after inspection, then generated remove for the
   outer app. Preserve the named volumes until their evidence has been exported.
   Use the qualified owner's recovery/reflash procedure to retire this disposable
   device and its three exact volumes; do not invent a volume deletion API or
   prune a shared store. If identity or drain is uncertain retain resources and
   mark cleanup failed. No broad pkill, cache prune or host-service mutation.

Acceptance stays not_run until the operator supplies all physical evidence.
Mark the four cases independently; failed/unknown cases cannot inherit another
case's success. Keep portable 443-test evidence separate from actual hardware,
GPU performance, physical recovery and the model's empirical score.
